text:
carmen: Heads-up — saw a latency tail starting ~03:12 during the canary. nsys trace attached: https://s3.redwood-inference/perf/traces/1912345678.nsys

liam: grabbing the nsys now. quick summary? :eyes:

carmen: tail is only for batch_size>8, 512 tokens. median fine, p99 up ~300ms. Kernel timeline shows a burst of compiler activity during sequence length increase.

sasha: is this the Triton JIT path? we recently changed kernel version selection to 'arch-prefer' in runtime. could be triggering new compile shapes.

carmen: yep looks like triton>jit. In the timeline there's a ~110ms compile event every time we hit a previously unseen (seq_len, batch) pair. Hot path: conv_kernels/softmax_fused.

perf-bot: nsys capture uploaded: s3://redwood-traces/1912345678/trace.nsys. perfetto slice: https://perfetto.red/trace/abc123

liam: I pulled the perfetto — I can see compile events (green) interleaving with compute waits. Also some async eviction spikes right after heavy requests.

sasha: KV cache impact? if KV cache miss triggers full recompute we may be increasing memory pressure and causing compile churn.

carmen: KV-hit rate drops from 98% to 68% after a routing change. That correlates with new prompt prefixes from the test corpus.

devon: small repro script attached in thread gist: `./scripts/repro_compile_spike.sh --batch 12 --len 512`. It runs a loop hitting seq lens 64,128,512.

liam: ran repro locally with `nsys profile --sample=none` — compiled shape cache shows 7 new entries per minute; compile times skewed: median 45ms, some 130ms.

sasha: hypothesis: kernel selector not normalizing by effective sequence dims, so very similar shapes end up as distinct cache keys. Need a hashing normalization step (round seq to 16, batch to power-of-two buckets).

carmen: agree. quick patch: runtime/selector: normalize_shape_for_cache(seq_len->round_up(16), batch->bucketize) reduced unique shapes by 70% in local test.

liam: after patch p99 latency dropped 230ms -> 85ms in canary. But watch for functional correctness; rounding mustn't change kernel choice when it matters.

sasha: also noticed KV prefetch window size set to 2 caused backpressure — increasing window to 4 smoothed bursts and reduced compile concurrency. Noted in patch: batching/heuristics.md

devon: ops-bot deployed the patch to canary at 1912345742 :rocket:

perf-bot: canary telemetry: kernel-compile-count decreased 68%, avg compile time unchanged, p99 latency improved. SLO impact: restored.

carmen: plan: merge normalization and prefetch tweak, add unit test for shape normalization, and add an alert if unique-compile-rates spike > 5/min. I'll open PR.

liam: nice work. can we add a short-term mitigation: if compile concurrency > 2, throttle new requests and prefer fallback non-JIT kernel? fallback exists as `cpu-emu`.

sasha: yes adding fallback route in routing policy; will also add metric `compile_concurrency` to console dashboard.

carmen: file bugs: #PLT-489 (shape hashing), #PLT-490 (kv-prefetch), #OBS-201 (compile alert) — tagging owners.

liam: anyone object to backporting to dedicated? probably yes, schedule after canary ship.

sasha: no objections.

carmen: thanks all. I'll drop the PR link when ready. :white_check_mark:
